name: GPS Broadcast Path & Ledger Depth Flywheel
description: Drives operator activation by removing all friction from the first GPS ping: a zero-auth sub-200KB driver PWA broadcasts location over 3G with IndexedDB offline queuing, each ping is written to PostgreSQL and atomically enqueued for Hyperledger Fabric ledger inscription, V/T ratio instrumentation in PostHog surfaces fleet coverage health, and a compliance-framed free-tier gate with loss-aversion copy converts operators who reach Day 28 of ledger history into paid subscribers. Upstash Redis delayed jobs fire Hour-4 and Hour-24 SMS nudges to accounts with no first ping, cancelling automatically on activation. The flywheel: more pings → deeper ledger history → stronger compliance narrative → higher upgrade conversion → more operators onboarded → more pings.

functions.name: POST
functions.logic: Extracts the JSON body from the incoming request containing fields: device_token (string), vehicle_id (string), lat (number), lng (number), accuracy (number), timestamp (ISO string), org_id (string). Validates device_token against the devices table in PostgreSQL — returns 401 if invalid. Derives cell_tower_fallback boolean as accuracy >= 50. Inserts a row into trip_events with columns: vehicle_id, org_id, lat, lng, accuracy, cell_tower_fallback, timestamp, created_at. After successful insert, calls enqueueHyperledgerWrite(pingPayload) to add a Fabric write job to the job queue. Checks if this is the first ping for org_id by querying trip_events count; if count equals 1, calls cancelNudgeJobs(org_id) to remove Upstash delayed SMS jobs, and emits a PostHog server event 'gps_first_ping_received' with properties org_id, vehicle_id, timestamp. Returns 200 JSON with trip_event_id and ledger_job_id. Returns 400 on malformed body, 500 on database error with structured error JSON.

functions.name: writeTripEvent
functions.signature: writeTripEvent(ping: GpsPingPayload): Promise<{ txId: string; timestamp: string }>
functions.logic: Accepts a GpsPingPayload object with fields: vehicle_id, org_id, lat, lng, accuracy, cell_tower_fallback, timestamp, trip_event_id. Constructs a Hyperledger Fabric transaction payload object mapping these fields plus a derived route_corridor string (computed from lat/lng against a static corridor lookup or passed as a field), an accuracy_flag string ('GPS' if cell_tower_fallback is false, 'CELL_TOWER' if true), and a unix epoch timestamp. Connects to the Fabric gateway using pre-loaded identity credentials from environment variables FABRIC_CERT, FABRIC_KEY, FABRIC_MSP_ID, FABRIC_PEER_ENDPOINT. Submits the transaction to the chaincode function 'recordTripEvent' on channel 'trip-channel'. On success, returns an object with txId (the Fabric transaction ID string) and timestamp (ISO string of block commit time). On Fabric SDK error, throws a structured FabricWriteError with code, message, and original error attached. Implements a single retry with 2-second backoff on transient GRPC errors.

functions.name: computeVTRatio
functions.logic: Accepts an orgId string and a date string in YYYY-MM-DD format. Executes a DuckDB query (or PostgreSQL equivalent) over the trip_events table joining against expected_trip_windows table, grouping by vehicle_id, counting distinct trip windows covered (actual_windows) versus total expected windows for that date (expected_windows), computing ratio as actual_windows / expected_windows. Returns an array of VTRatioResult objects each containing: vehicle_id (string), org_id (string), date (string), vt_ratio (number between 0 and 1), actual_windows (number), expected_windows (number), below_threshold (boolean, true if vt_ratio < 0.5). For each result, emits a PostHog server-side event 'vehicle_vt_ratio_updated' with properties vehicle_id, org_id, date, vt_ratio, below_threshold using the PostHog server client from src/lib/server/posthog.ts. Vehicles with below_threshold true are additionally written to a Redis set key 'vt_flagged:{date}:{orgId}' for consumption by the 6AM WhatsApp briefing job. Handles division-by-zero when expected_windows is 0 by setting vt_ratio to null and below_threshold to false.

functions.name: enqueueActivationNudges
functions.signature: enqueueActivationNudges(orgId: string, phoneNumber: string): Promise<{ job4hId: string; job24hId: string }>
functions.logic: Accepts orgId (string) and phoneNumber (E.164 format string) for the operator contact. Creates two Upstash QStash or Redis delayed jobs: the first with a delay of 4 hours (14400 seconds) and the second with a delay of 24 hours (86400 seconds) from the current time. Each job payload contains: org_id, phone_number, nudge_type ('hour_4' or 'hour_24'), created_at. Stores both job IDs in a Redis hash key 'nudge_jobs:{orgId}' with fields 'job_4h' and 'job_24h' so they can be cancelled later. The SMS content for hour_4 nudge is activation-focused ('Your fleet is ready — send your first GPS ping to start compliance tracking'). The SMS content for hour_24 nudge is compliance-framed ('24h passed without GPS data. Kenyan transport compliance requires trip records — activate now to protect your licence'). Returns an object with job4hId and job24hId strings. Throws EnqueueError if Upstash client fails.

functions.name: cancelNudgeJobs
functions.logic: Accepts orgId string. Retrieves the Redis hash at key 'nudge_jobs:{orgId}' to fetch job_4h and job_24h job IDs. For each job ID that exists and is non-null, calls the Upstash QStash DELETE endpoint or Redis job cancellation API to remove the scheduled job. Deletes the Redis hash key 'nudge_jobs:{orgId}' after cancellation attempts. Logs a warning (does not throw) if a job ID is missing or cancellation returns a 404 (job may have already fired). Returns void. Safe to call multiple times (idempotent).

functions.name: flushQueue
functions.logic: Opens the IndexedDB database 'gps_queue' and reads all pending ping records from the 'pings' object store ordered by timestamp ascending. For each record, attempts an HTTP POST to the GPS ping ingest endpoint /api/gps/ping with the stored payload and the device_token from localStorage. On successful 200 response, deletes the record from IndexedDB. On network failure, stops flushing and leaves remaining records for the next flush cycle. Registers a listener on the browser 'online' event to call flushQueue automatically when connectivity is restored. Also called once on component mount to drain any queue accumulated during a previous offline session. Handles IndexedDB errors gracefully by logging to console without crashing the PWA.

functions.name: POST
functions.logic: Extracts JSON body with fields: operator_id (string), plan_id (string), phone_number (E.164 string). Constructs an idempotency key as 'mpesa_upgrade:{operator_id}:{plan_id}' and checks Upstash Redis for an existing value — if found and not expired, returns 409 with the existing STK push request_id to prevent duplicate charges. Queries the ledger_events table to fetch ledger_event_count and computes days_since_first_ping for the operator to pre-populate the STK push description with compliance context. Calls the Safaricom Daraja STK Push API (BusinessShortCode, LipaNaMpesaOnlineURL) with the plan amount, phone_number, account_reference set to operator_id, and transaction_description including ledger event count. On Daraja success (ResponseCode '0'), stores the CheckoutRequestID in Redis under the idempotency key with a 24-hour TTL. Returns 200 JSON with checkout_request_id and merchant_request_id. Returns 400 on validation failure, 502 on Daraja API error with structured error details.

integrations.description: Hyperledger Fabric ledger: GPS pings are written as immutable ledger transactions via the Fabric SDK, providing the compliance audit trail that powers the upgrade gate narrative. Requires FABRIC_CERT, FABRIC_KEY, FABRIC_MSP_ID, FABRIC_PEER_ENDPOINT environment variables.
integrations.verification: curl -X POST http://localhost:5173/api/gps/ping -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"device_token":"test","vehicle_id":"v1","lat":-1.286389,"lng":36.817223,"accuracy":10,"timestamp":"2024-01-01T08:00:00Z","org_id":"org1"}' && grep 'txId' logs/fabric.log

integrations.description: Upstash Redis: used for delayed SMS nudge job scheduling (Hour-4 and Hour-24), job cancellation on first ping, M-Pesa upgrade idempotency keys, and V/T ratio flagged vehicle sets. Requires UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN environment variables.

Safaricom Daraja STK Push API: initiates M-Pesa payment prompts for free-tier upgrade conversion. Requires DARAJA_CONSUMER_KEY, DARAJA_CONSUMER_SECRET, DARAJA_SHORTCODE, DARAJA_PASSKEY, DARAJA_CALLBACK_URL environment variables.

GPS ping ingest endpoint at /api/gps/ping: receives POST requests from the driver PWA with device_token, vehicle_id, coordinates, accuracy, and org_id. Central activation trigger for the entire growth loop.

FreeTierLedgerGate.svelte: compliance-framed upgrade prompt surfaced at Day 28 of ledger history. Queries ledger_event_count and days_until_cap, renders KES protection estimate, and triggers the M-Pesa STK push flow.

PostHog server-side analytics: receives vehicle_vt_ratio_updated events from the V/T computation cycle and gps_first_ping_received activation events. Uses the existing server-side PostHog client at src/lib/server/posthog.ts.

telemetry.description: Fires on the first GPS ping INSERT into trip_events for an org — this is the core activation milestone of the entire flywheel. Capturing it at the database level ensures no ping is missed regardless of application-layer failures, and it is the primary signal for Time-to-First-GPS-Ping < 48h success metric tracking.

success_criteria: Time to First GPS Ping < 48 hours for > 60% of new operator accounts, measured from account created_at to first trip_events INSERT timestamp
Driver PWA initial load time < 4 seconds on Safaricom 3G (measured via Lighthouse CI on 3G throttle profile)
Driver PWA static bundle size < 200KB (measured post-build via du on .svelte-kit/output/client)
Zero GPS ping data loss due to connectivity drop: IndexedDB queue flush success rate = 100% verified by comparing pings_queued vs trip_events rows per device session
Hyperledger Fabric write success rate > 99.5% per GPS ping ingested, measured as successful_fabric_txns / total_trip_events_inserted over rolling 7-day window
V/T ratio > 0.75 across active fleet portfolio at Month 2, measured as median vt_ratio across all vehicles with >= 10 expected_trip_windows in the period
Free-tier ledger gate upgrade conversion > 15% measured as mpesa_upgrade_initiated / free_tier_gate_prompt_displayed within 7 days of prompt
Hour-4 SMS nudge delivery rate > 95% for accounts with no first ping, measured via SMS gateway delivery receipts
Hour-24 SMS nudge to first ping conversion > 20% for accounts that received the 24h nudge but had not yet pinged
Operator activation rate (first GPS ping within 48h) improves by >= 25 percentage points within 60 days of loop deployment
